newsitem.title: USA: Unemployment rate drops in Vermont, state revenues.
newsitem.headline: Unemployment rate drops in Vermont, state revenues.

text.p: Vermont's unemployment rate dropped to a seasonally adjusted 3.9 percent in January -- the lowest jobless rate in the state since September 1989, Vermont Department Employment and Training said.
The January figure is a sharp drop from December's 4.6 percent jobless rate, but offiials warned the January figure could be revised upward.
Monthly unemployment figures are preliminary and subject to review, the DET said.

"Unemployment appeared to improve in January, but the drop may be slightly overstated," DET Commissioner Susan Auld said. "Jobs data obtained from an independent DET survey showed continued modest growth in the Vermont economy, largely in the trade and service industries."
Meanwhile, Vermont officials reported that winter's warmer weather may lead to lower tax revenues as the skiing resorts reported a moderate season.
Of course that season may be extended after Thursday's storm dumped up to 20-inches of snow in central and northern Vermont.

Administraton Secretary Bill Sorrell said that other taxes were within $1 million of projections, but he indicated that state income tax returns may be larger this year than anticipated and that too could drain the state coffers as well.
